name: Superteam Earn World Cup hackathon powered by TxODDS / TxLINE
theme: Real-time sports data and decentralized applications on Solana for the World Cup
required_or_encouraged_tech: TxLINE data as primary live input
CPI into TxLINE validate_stat (optional, encouraged for Track 1)

facts.claim: Submission window is June 24, 2026 15:00 UTC to July 19, 2026 23:59 UTC.
Winner announcement on July 29, 2026 15:00 UTC.
Team size maximum 3.
Required submission: working build, demo video up to 5 min, public repo, deployed website or functional API/devnet endpoint, brief technical documentation, TxLINE endpoint list, and API feedback.
TxLINE provides high-performance data layer for real-time sports data and consensus betting odds.
TxLINE covers all 104 World Cup matches with normalized JSON schema.
TxLINE updates are cryptographically signed and anchored on Solana.
Hackathon builders receive free TxLINE access until the submission deadline.

Common requirements: TxLINE data must be a primary live input; products must be functional, not wireframes or pitch decks; demo video quality matters because live matches may not be active during judging.
Participants must comply with gambling, gaming, financial, consumer protection, and securities laws.
Track 1 (Prediction Markets and Settlement) prize pool: 18,000 USDT (1st 12k, 2nd 4k, 3rd 2k).
Track 1 observed submissions: 112.
Track 1 focuses on prediction platforms, sportsbook interfaces, data dashboards, decentralized prediction markets, AMMs, escrow settlement engines, parametric sports insurance, prop bets.

Track 1 judges value smooth TxLINE ingestion, compelling soccer/analytical UX, clean deterministic resolution/validation code, optional Merkle proof verification, custom Solana settlement logic using TxLINE validation primitives.
Track 1 constraint: TxLINE credit token cannot be used for user wagering or transfers; user funds can be held in other assets like USDC.
Track 1 encourages using TxLINE Merkle proofs and CPI into TxLINE validate_stat for trustless settlement.
Track 2 (Consumer and Fan Experiences) prize pool: 16,000 USDT (1st 10k, 2nd 4k, 3rd 2k).
Track 2 observed submissions: 113.
Track 2 focuses on mainstream fan products using live scores, odds, match events; example ideas: group sweepstakes, AI pundit bots, hi-lo stats games.
Track 2 judges value fan accessibility and polish, real-time responsiveness, original consumer interaction models, monetization path, complete end-to-end execution.
Track 2 extra requirement: sign up through Solana.
Track 3 (Trading Tools and Agents) prize pool: 16,000 USDT (1st 10k, 2nd 4k, 3rd 2k).
Track 3 observed submissions: 91.
Track 3 focuses on autonomous agents ingesting TxLINE feeds and executing defined strategies; example ideas: sharp movement detector, agent-vs-agent arena, in-play market maker.
Track 3 judges value core feed ingestion, autonomous operation, deterministic and mathematically defensible strategy logic, novelty, production readiness for trading teams.

inference.claim: Winning products must deeply integrate TxLINE live data, as it is the central dependency and judging criterion.
inference.rationale: TxLINE is specified as primary live input for all tracks, and judges explicitly value smooth ingestion.

inference.claim: High-quality demo videos with simulated real-time data are critical because live matches may not be active during judging.
inference.rationale: Common requirements stress demo video quality for that reason.

inference.claim: Projects with simple, well-scoped builds have an advantage given the short hackathon window (just under 4 weeks).
inference.rationale: Submission deadline is tight; extensive feature sets risk incomplete demos.

inference.claim: Track 1 carries higher legal/regulatory risk due to direct betting mechanics; judges will favor compliant designs or clearly separated non-wagerable demos.
inference.rationale: Explicit legal warnings and prohibition on TxLINE token wagering suggest compliance scrutiny.

inference.claim: Track 3 may have lower submission volume (91 observed) offering less direct competition, but requires strong algorithmic novelty.
inference.rationale: Emphasis on mathematically defensible strategies raises the technical bar; fewer submissions may mean higher quality.

inference.claim: Adding trustless settlement via Merkle proofs and CPI on Solana can be a differentiator in Track 1.
inference.rationale: Optional features are specifically mentioned as desirable by judges.

inference.claim: Mainstream consumer apps (Track 2) likely benefit from Solana-native sign-in to simplify UX and meet the requirement.
inference.rationale: Sign-up through Solana is mandatory; using it elegantly can improve polish.

inference.claim: The product must go beyond a simple dashboard; judges value original interaction models and end-to-end execution.
inference.rationale: Track 2 explicitly values 'original consumer interaction models' and 'complete end-to-end execution'.

inference.claim: Data dashboards alone are unlikely to win without real-time features or irreversible state changes.
inference.rationale: The brief warns against wireframes/pitch decks; a static dashboard may be seen as insufficient.

sanitized_brief: Build for the TxODDS World Cup Hackathon (powered by TxLINE) on Solana. Three tracks: Prediction Markets & Settlement (18k USDT), Consumer & Fan Experiences (16k USDT), Trading Tools & Agents (16k USDT). Deadline July 19, 2026; teams max 3. You must use TxLINE live sports data as primary input—it provides real-time scores, match events, and consensus odds for all 104 World Cup matches, all cryptographically signed and anchored on Solana. Free API access until deadline. Judging values smooth TxLINE integration, polished demo video, user experience, technical correctness, and novelty. Avoid high-collision archetypes: standard prediction markets, pundit bots, sweepstakes, sharp movement detectors, in-play market makers. Explore underexplored angles like trustless verification tools, real-time interactive games with irreversible state changes, compliance automation, or novel fan experiences. Do not build wireframes or non-functional dashboards. Ensure legal compliance—TxLINE token cannot be used for wagering. Prioritize buildable, demo-ready solutions with clear TxLINE dependency and low regulatory risk.
